items.title: [None][feat] Add Cosmos3 Edge Policy DROID support
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Adds native `nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge-Policy-DROID` support without changing the public request API.
- Loads policy metadata from `checkpoint.json` and applies validated DROID defaults.
- Reuses the Cosmos3 Action path for state conditioning and joint denoising.
- Returns 32 predicted 8-D actions and excludes the conditioned state row.
- Preserves scheduler flow shift, policy sampling, and caller-controlled prompt formatting.
- Adds Nemotron-dense backbone detection for incomplete export configurations.
- Removes obsolete `view_point` handling and action prompt synthesis.
- Supports structured JSON prompt objects and rejects unsupported prompt types.
- Extends serving serialization to include action tensors.
- Updates documentation, example prompts, CLI options, and checkpoint behavior.
- Adds validation for state dimensions, policy modes, metadata conflicts, and action output handling.
- Test-list changes use the correct B200 format and add the DROID example with a 20-minute timeout.
- Reported validation includes a native B300 build, 377 focused tests with 1 skipped, a real-checkpoint smoke test, and passing pre-commit checks.

## QA Engineer Review

- Added `test_cosmos3_edge_policy_droid_example` in `tests/integration/defs/examples/visual_gen/test_visual_gen_cosmos3.py`.
- Added `TestCheckpointPolicyDefaults` and policy-state preparation coverage in `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_action.py`.
- Added backbone detection, registry, and policy-default coverage in `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_edge.py`.
- Added structured prompt and DROID prompt coverage in `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_example_prompts.py`.
- Extended serving endpoint tests in `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_trtllm_serve_endpoints.py` for action tensors, batching, serialization, and checkpoint requests.
- The integration test is covered by `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_b200.yml`.
- Unit tests are not listed separately in `test-db/` or `qa/`; CI coverage for those tests is not confirmed.
- Verdict: needs follow-up.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Add native VisualGen support for `nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge-Policy-DROID` without changing the public request API.

- Read the checkpoint's Policy metadata (`action_chunk_size`, conditioning FPS, and domain) from `checkpoint.json`, and apply the remaining DROID Policy recipe defaults only for `droid_lerobot`.
- Reuse the existing Cosmos3 Action path for current-state conditioning and joint video/action denoising, returning the 32 predicted 8-D actions without the clean state-conditioning row.
- Preserve the checkpoint scheduler flow shift and Policy sampling recipe instead of inheriting regular Edge video defaults.
- Infer the existing Nemotron-dense architecture only from the released export's complete signature when `backbone_type` is absent.
- Keep prompt formatting request-owned: the example client can serialize a caller-provided nested JSON object, while the pipeline continues to accept and forward strings unchanged.
- Add the example request, serving documentation, integration coverage, and focused unit coverage. Existing `input_reference`, `extra_params`, and tensor response formats carry all Policy inputs and outputs.

## Test Coverage

- Native B300 build after merging `upstream/main`: `gpu-run` run `20260831-141337-284726` succeeded.
- Focused post-merge suite:
  `pytest -q tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_edge.py tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_action.py tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_example_prompts.py tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_trtllm_serve_endpoints.py`
  (`377 passed, 1 skipped`).
- Real `nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge-Policy-DROID` checkpoint smoke test on B300: generated video `(33, 544, 736, 3)` and action `(32, 8)` at 15 FPS using Policy mode.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD` passed.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Updated `TestKimiK3.test_w4a16_mxfp4` documentation.
- Added baseline and `sa` Kimi K3 GSM8K entries to the GB300 16-GPU, 4-node PyTorch post-merge stage.

- Reuse and MMMU tests remain in the weekly QA pipeline.
- Configuration and test-list changes are consistent with the stated CI scope.
- No correctness, API, or error-handling issues were identified.

**Verdict: sufficient**

## QA Engineer Review

- Modified `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300_multi_nodes_node4_gpu16.yml`.
- Added:
  - `TestKimiK3::test_w4a16_mxfp4[baseline]`
  - `TestKimiK3::test_w4a16_mxfp4[sa]`
- No test entries were removed.
- The modified test function is covered in `test-db/`.
- Reuse and MMMU modes remain covered only by the weekly QA pipeline.
- CBTS coverage data is unavailable.

**Verdict: needs follow-up**
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Kimi K3 has had no accuracy guard in automated CI: the 16-GPU GSM8K/MMMU accuracy tests added in #17922 are registered only in QA's weekly multinode list, so an accuracy regression would surface up to a week after the offending merge. #18363 just introduced GB300 multi-node post-merge stages, including the 16-GPU 4-node `GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-SingleNvlinkDomain-Post-Merge-1` stage — exactly the topology the K3 tests were qualified on (4x4 GB300, one NVLink domain).

This PR registers the two highest-value K3 GSM8K legs in that stage:

- `accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py::TestKimiK3::test_w4a16_mxfp4[baseline]` — the core GSM8K accuracy guard.
- `accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py::TestKimiK3::test_w4a16_mxfp4[sa]` — the same guard under suffix-automaton speculative decoding, which also asserts the acceptance-length baseline (`references/acceptance_length.yaml`).

Both entries get `TIMEOUT (120)`, matching the stage's existing 16-GPU entry; the values can be tightened once the stage produces real timings.

Notes:

- The tests run **as-is** (DEP16): the configuration and its reference baselines are exactly what QA already validated on 4x4 GB300 nodes, so no test-logic changes and no reference changes are needed.
- The `reuse` and MMMU legs deliberately stay QA-weekly-only for now (post-merge cost control); the QA list `qa/llm_function_multinode.txt` keeps all four K3 entries, i.e. the same dual registration #18363 used for the Qwen3.8 tests.
- No Jenkins changes: the stage already exists (splits=1) and `l0_gb300_multi_nodes_node4_gpu16.yml` is already listed in `getMultiGpuFileChanged`. Per #18363's design, entries are added to the existing per-topology list rather than a new one, because `scripts/test_to_stage_mapping.py` resolves stage ↔ test by list name.
- The test docstring is refreshed (it claimed no automated stage schedules 16-GPU tests), and the B300-exclusion comment now notes the CI stage's gb300-only gpu wildcard enforces that exclusion on the CI side.

Sanity check: `python3 scripts/test_to_stage_mapping.py --tests "accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py::TestKimiK3::test_w4a16_mxfp4[baseline]" "accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py::TestKimiK3::test_w4a16_mxfp4[sa]"` resolves both entries to `GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-SingleNvlinkDomain-Post-Merge-1`.

## Test Coverage

- The wiring itself is exercised by running the new stage on this PR:
  `/bot run --disable-fail-fast --extra-stage "GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-SingleNvlinkDomain-Post-Merge-1"`
  (post-merge stages do not run on PRs by default). That run is the first in-CI execution of the K3 legs; the test configuration itself was previously validated by QA at this exact topology.
- Guarded tests after merge: `TestKimiK3::test_w4a16_mxfp4[baseline]` and `[sa]` run on every merged PR alongside the stage's existing Qwen3.8 entry.

items.title: [None][fix] Support fixed-only draft KV cache budgets
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- The change preserves KV cache costs as affine slope/intercept values.
- The budget splitter reserves fixed target and draft costs before proportional slope allocation.
- The DFlash V2 estimator includes retained SWA boundary pages, generation headroom, context slots, and the slot-aligned float32 resume watermark.
- Estimator dependencies now use explicit parameters.
- Error handling covers insufficient capacity and exact fixed-budget cases.
- The public method signature remains compatible because `**kwargs` is retained.
- No configuration files or test-list files changed.
- The implementation is consistent with the stated scope. No correctness or regression issues are identified from the supplied changes.

## QA Engineer Review

Test-code changes include:

- Updated `test_kv_cache_budget_split.py` to model affine cache costs.
- Added coverage for fixed-only draft costs.
- Added coverage for fixed-only target and draft managers.
- Added coverage for target fixed costs with linear draft costs.
- Added rejection coverage when a linear manager cannot fit within an exact fixed GPU budget.
- Added a DFlash estimation regression test in `test_kv_cache_estimation.py`.
- Updated LagunaXS DFlash BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 accuracy helpers to enable KV cache manager V2.

The supplied summary reports 79 focused unit tests and successful LagunaXS 2:1 DFlash accuracy cases for all three precisions. Test-list coverage is not identified in the supplied changes.

**Verdict: needs follow-up.**
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

LagunaXS uses a separate DFlash draft cache whose layers are all sliding-window attention. Its cache cost is fixed per request with zero per-token slope. The V2 target/draft budget splitter previously rejected zero slopes, so both managers inherited the full profiled GPU budget and creating the draft manager could raise `CuOOM`.

This change keeps cache costs as a pure affine `(slope, intercept)` contract and supports fixed-only managers by reserving both intercepts before distributing the remaining budget by slope. The DFlash V2 estimator now includes the retained SWA boundary page, speculative generation headroom, context slots, and the slot-aligned float32 resume watermark in the fixed quota it reports. Estimator dependencies are explicit function parameters; no separate allocation-unit field is introduced.

The existing LagunaXS BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 DFlash accuracy cases now enable KV cache manager V2 as end-to-end regression coverage.

## Test Coverage

- Focused KV cache budget/estimation unit tests: `79 passed`
- Pre-commit hooks on all modified files: passed
- B200 LagunaXS 2:1 DFlash with KVCM V2:
  - BF16: passed; MMLU 76.17, GSM8K 87.38
  - FP8: passed; MMLU 76.10, GSM8K 87.98
  - NVFP4: passed; MMLU 75.66, GSM8K 83.97

## PR Checklist

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

items.title: [None][fix] warn when tool parser matches marker but extracts no calls
items.body:
## Description
When a tool parser matches its marker (`has_tool_call(text)` is true) but extracts zero calls (e.g. due to malformed JSON, empty tool block, or parser/template mismatch), the request returns HTTP 200 with an empty `tool_calls` array without any diagnostic in the logs.

This PR emits a `logger.warning` on that non-streaming path in both Chat Completions (`postprocess_handlers.py`) and Responses API (`responses_utils.py`), naming the configured parser and listing plausible causes.

Fixes #17917

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Test Plan
- Added unit tests in `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_tool_parsers.py` (`TestToolParserEmptyExtractionWarning`):
  - Verified warning is logged on marker match with zero extractions (naming configured parser).
  - Verified no warning on plain text responses.
  - Verified no warning on valid tool extractions.
  - Verified no warning on streaming chunks.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Added log-only warnings for non-streaming Chat Completions and Responses API tool-parser paths.
- Warnings identify the configured parser and plausible causes.
- Existing API responses and parsing behavior remain unchanged.
- No configuration, public entity, or test-list changes were identified.

## QA Engineer Review

- Tests cover empty extraction, plain text, valid tool calls, streaming chunks, and disabled diagnostics.

items.title: [None][feat] perf-sanity: upload per-request disagg lifecycle spans to OpenSearch
items.body:
## Summary

Disagg perf-sanity uploads only *aggregate* client-side metrics today (TTFT, ITL, TPOT, throughput). When TTFT regresses, OpenSearch gives no indication of *which lifecycle phase* moved — ctx queueing, prefill, the KV-cache relay, gen admission, or the response relay back.

`tensorrt_llm/serve/scripts/time_breakdown` already decomposes each disagg request into **12 contiguous lifecycle spans**, but it is human-only: it renders an HTML chart and prints Range/Median.

This PR adds a disagg benchmark mode, **`e2e_time_breakdown`**, that runs the workload **once** and uploads **27 metrics × 4 statistics (mean / median / p75 / p99) = 108 `d_tb_<metric>_<stat>` fields** alongside the normal metrics — giving the dashboard a per-phase latency history that can be bisected.

First case:

```
disagg_upload-e2e_time_breakdown-gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-fp4_8k1k_con666_ctx6_dep4_gen1_dep16_eplb384_mtp3_ccb-NIXL
```

The new metrics are registered in `MINIMIZE_METRICS` but **deliberately not** in `REGRESSION_METRICS` — they are diagnostic and can never fail a stage. (`perf_regression_utils` asserts `REGRESSION_METRICS ⊆ MAXIMIZE ∪ MINIMIZE`, so the `MINIMIZE_METRICS` registration is mandatory; it skips metrics absent from `new_data`, so no existing case is affected.)

A second, smaller metric addition rides on the same upload path and is described under **Also in this PR** below: five per-iter gen-worker device-step-time columns for `e2e` (and `e2e_time_breakdown`), uploaded and baselined but never gating — plus a latent per-client windowing bug fixed on the way.

## What gets uploaded, and for which case types

`tests/integration/defs/perf/time_breakdown_metrics.py` (new, stdlib-only so test collection never imports `tensorrt_llm`) parses the per-request JSONL and returns the full metric set for a given case type:

| group | metrics | `ctx_only` | `gen_only` | `e2e` |
|---|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 1 · Context/prefill stage | `ctx_preprocessing`, `ctx_queue`, `ctx_processing`, `ctx_postprocessing` | ✅ | — | ✅ |
| 2 · Per-chunk prefill | `chunk_{preprocessing,forward,update,sample,postprocessing}`, `chunk_gpu_{forward,sample}` | ✅ | — | ✅ |
| 3 · Per-step generation | `step_{preprocessing,forward,update,sample,postprocessing}`, `step_gpu_{forward,sample}` | — | ✅ | ✅ |
| 4 · Generation/decode stage | `gen_{preprocessing,queue,postprocessing}`, `gen_{queue_wait,kv_transfer,post_transfer}` | — | ✅ | ✅ |
| 5 · Disagg server | `disagg_{preprocessing,relay,postprocessing}` | — | ✅ | ✅ |

Only disagg cases are supported; aggregated cases have no breakdown. An unsupported group uploads **`0.0` rather than being omitted**, so the OpenSearch doc schema is identical on every row and a column never appears or disappears depending on mode — a missing field and a zero are very different things to chart, and only one of them is greppable. Non-chunked prefill still reports group 2, treated as a single chunk.

Two free internal consistency checks fall out of the decomposition and are asserted in tests: the five `chunk_*` CPU spans sum exactly to `ctx_processing`, and `gen_queue_wait + gen_kv_transfer + gen_post_transfer` sums exactly to `gen_queue`.

## Multiple ctx / gen workers — and a bug found while handling them

A case has N ctx and M gen workers, each writing its own JSONL. Three things this requires:

- **Role cannot come from the filename.** Every worker writes kind `server` (`server_role` is `None` ⇒ `openai_server.py` falls back to `"server"`), so `perf_metrics-<role>-*.jsonl` files do not exist. Role is resolved by *content*: `ctx_chunk_metrics` ⇒ ctx, `step_metrics` ⇒ gen. Note `kv_cache_transfer_start` is present on the **ctx** side too (send side); only `kv_cache_transfer_end`/`kv_cache_size` are gen-exclusive, so the obvious discriminator is wrong.
- **Samples are pooled**, not averaged per worker then averaged again — a mean-of-means would silently reweight an unbalanced worker.
- **Clock bases differ per worker process.** `ctx_chunk_metrics`/`step_metrics` timestamps use a different monotonic origin than `perf_metrics.timing_metrics`. The offset is constant per process but varies wildly across processes: measured on real GB300 hardware, the ctx worker sat at **+294065.985 s** and the four gen workers at **+0.0003 / +377680.565 / +9.9706 / +0.9927 s**.

The first implementation estimated **one** offset per file. That is correct for a per-worker file and **wrong for the merged/combined file**, which mixes all workers together — it corrupts the first instance's preprocessing for N−1 of them (`step_preprocessing_mean` read −17.6703 ms merged vs −11.7187 ms from raw worker files). A ±60 s plausibility guard caught the +377680 s worker but **silently passed the +9.97 s and +0.99 s ones**, which is the worse failure mode precisely because the result still looks plausible. Fixed by partitioning records by worker process (`ctx_server`/`gen_server` for a combined record, file path for a worker file) and estimating an offset per worker: 0 disagreements across all 108 fields, plus a warning when the spread exceeds 1 s. Mutation-tested — reverting the partition makes exactly the one regression test fail.

Only the **first** instance's preprocessing crosses the clock boundary (it is anchored at `first_scheduled_time`); intra-array spans are base-invariant. If a worker has too few requests to pin its offset (< 3), that single crossing value is **dropped rather than emitted raw**, so an unverifiable estimate can never inject a multi-day outlier into a millisecond distribution.

`ctx_only` runs its worker in *aggregated* mode (`disagg_run_type: "aggr"`, no disagg server), so no merged file exists at all; groups 1–2 are computed straight off the lone worker file. Only group 5 needs the cross-role join.

## Two transport defects fixed first — without them the spans would be *wrong*, not missing

Since worker→disagg per-request timing became Server-Timing header strings, that transport is lossy:

1. **4 of 6 absolute timestamps were never forwarded.** `build_metrics_headers` emitted only `arrival_time` and `last_token_time`; `server_arrival_time`, `server_first_token_time`, `kv_cache_transfer_start` and `kv_cache_transfer_end` were dropped. `RequestDataParser` then *silently* substitutes fallbacks, and `calculate_duration` returns `0` on `nan`.
2. **A second-order strip defeated the fix for (1).** `_jsonl_perf_metrics` popped the KV-transfer timestamps whenever `timing_metrics["kv_cache_size"]` was falsy — and `kv_cache_size` is worker-local, never reaching a header-derived record. Extending the header transport alone still yielded a zero-width KV span.

Measured on unmodified `main`, **10 of 12 spans were wrong, and 4 of the wrong values were non-zero and plausible** — i.e. they would pass a dashboard eyeball test:

| span | before | true |
|---|---|---|
| `gen_postprocessing` | 145.0 ms | 11.0 ms |
| `disagg_relay` | 18.0 ms | 6.0 ms |
| `disagg_preprocessing` | 3.0 ms | 1.0 ms |
| 5 spans | 0 (nan → 0) | non-zero |

After the fix: **12/12 exact**, now covered by unit tests. This repairs `--save-request-time-breakdown` for **every** disagg user, not just perf-sanity.

New header tokens are named `srv-start` / `srv-ttft` / `kv-start` / `kv-end` because the disagg server rewrites the phase prefix with an unqualified `str.replace("server-", f"{phase}-")`; any token containing a second `server-` would be double-substituted. Header cost is ~260 bytes against an 80 KiB budget. A peer that does not emit the new tokens degrades to exactly today's behaviour (covered by a backward-compat test).

## Validated end to end on real hardware

One `8k1k_con8_ctx1_dep4_gen4_tep8_eplb0_mtp3_ccb-NIXL` run on GB300 (1 ctx + 4 gen workers, 80 requests, 18480 recorded steps), fed through the real parser → log formatter → harness regex → upload path:

```
d_tb_ctx_processing_mean       623.9996      d_tb_gen_queue_mean         2598.3722
d_tb_chunk_forward_mean        329.8308      d_tb_disagg_relay_mean         9.4765
d_tb_step_preprocessing_mean   -11.7187      d_tb_step_gpu_forward_mean    12.3933
```

108 fields uploaded, all in `MINIMIZE_METRICS`, none in `REGRESSION_METRICS`; the 10 lifecycle spans sum to 3459.2066 ms after a full format→regex round trip. `gen_only` on the same data zeroes exactly 44 fields (groups 1+2 = 11 metrics × 4 stats).

`step_preprocessing` is **legitimately negative** under the overlap scheduler (step *N* forwards before step *N−1*'s `token_time`). It is a signed term of a contiguous decomposition, so it is reported as-is rather than clamped — and the harness regex accepts a leading `-`, without which exactly the metric that proves overlap is working would be dropped on every row, forever.

The 12 lifecycle spans tile **TTFT, not E2E** (decode is excluded), which makes `sum == TTFT` a free parse check.

## Also included

- **`num_postprocess_workers: 0`** on the workers for this mode, which keeps the breakdown structured. It measurably changes throughput, so the case lands on its **own** `s_test_case_name` series with its own baselines and its aggregate numbers are **deliberately not comparable** to the sibling `e2e` case.
- Benchmark-mode whitelists widened in both submit generators **and** in `cache_transceiver_precheck/run_precheck.py` — `submit.py` pastes the mode token into `pytestCommand{CTX,GEN}Precheck` verbatim, so a missing `choices` entry would have killed the precheck srun *before the workload started*, with a message that reads as a launch failure.
- `testCount` 2 → 3 for the ctx6 stage family (`submit.py` hard-fails if `testCount` ≠ the number of tests). Measured group mapping with `--splits 3 --splitting-algorithm=least_duration`: `-1` = `e2e`, **`-2` = `e2e_time_breakdown`**, `-3` = `gen_only`.
- Mode → case-type is mapped **explicitly with no default**: a mode falling through to an unsupported case type would upload 108 zeros and look exactly like a run that measured nothing.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/others/test_time_breakdown_metrics.py` (**new**, 13 tests) — schema stability across modes, per-mode gating, the chunk/`ctx_processing` and `gen_queue` sum identities, negative `step_preprocessing` under overlap, `ctx_only` without a disagg server, 0/NaN timestamps excluded rather than counted as zero-width spans, role classified by content not filename, and two dedicated clock-base tests: **per-worker correction across four workers at the real measured offsets** (interleaved round-robin, compared stat-for-stat against a single-worker zero-offset reference) and the conservative drop when an offset cannot be estimated.
- `tests/unittest/others/test_perf_sanity_time_breakdown.py` (14 tests) — every tool span is known to the harness, metric-name coverage, log-line ↔ regex round trip for **both** producers including the 6-decimal negative value, every mapped mode is one the parser supports, diagnostic-only registration, and mode-gated upload.
- `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_request_metrics.py` (+5 tests) — all 6 timestamps survive the header round trip for both phases; no double-substituted phase prefix; the KV timestamps are kept when present and still stripped when absent; a header-derived combined record yields **12 non-zero spans** (the direct regression test for both defects); span statistics are in ms.
- `tests/unittest/others/test_cache_transceiver_precheck_config.py` (+2 tests) — every forwarded mode is accepted, and an unknown mode is still rejected.

Verified offline: exactly 2 new parametrised ids and 0 removed; the full parsed-config diff against the `e2e` sibling is exactly the 3 worker keys + 1 client flag + the mode/name strings, with `hardware:` untouched; the generated `slurm_launch.sh` differs only in group index, output dir and `--benchmark-mode`, with topology unchanged at 10 nodes / 40 GPUs.

## Also in this PR: gen-worker device step time for `e2e`

A second, smaller metric addition on the same upload path.

Disagg `e2e` uploads only *aggregate client-side* metrics (TTFT, ITL, TPOT, throughput). When one of those regresses, the row carries no device-side number, so a decode slowdown cannot be told from host or transport cost — and `host_step_time` cannot stand in for it, because over the same loop body it agrees with `prev_device_step_time` by identity.

`gen_only` already publishes five per-iter `prev_device_step_time` statistics scraped from `gen_server_*.log`. This forwards the same family to **`e2e` and `e2e_time_breakdown`** via a new `DEVICE_STEP_TIME_MODES` tuple:

| mode | uploaded | gates (`b_is_regression`) |
|---|:-:|:-:|
| `gen_only` | all 5 | `d_{mean,median}_...` (unchanged) |
| `e2e` | all 5 | **none** |
| `e2e_time_breakdown` | all 5 | **none** |
| `ctx_only` | — | — |

The "uploaded but never gating" half needs no code and is worth being explicit about, because the two lists are independent: `MINIMIZE_METRICS` membership buys a baseline and an `s_regression_info` diff line, while only membership in the `regression_metrics` *argument* can set `b_is_regression`. `e2e` takes the `else` branch and gets the default `REGRESSION_METRICS` (throughput), which contains no `gen_worker` name — so there the five are structurally incapable of failing a build, while still accruing history. `gen_only` keeps its `GEN_ONLY_REGRESSION_METRICS` override, where token throughput is dominated by KV-cache transfer and is not a useful signal. Asserted as a test rather than left to inspection.

`ctx_only` is excluded **by construction**, not by policy: it runs the *aggregated* runtime from a disagg yaml with no gen worker, so no `gen_server_*.log` exists. TTFT is the prefill signal there and already uploads on every mode.

A missing value **omits the columns rather than failing the run**, except in `gen_only` where the family is the only regression signal and the existing hard fail stands. Hard-failing elsewhere would turn a diagnostic addition into a new red-build mode for every `e2e` case on every cluster, gated on log-scrape plumbing rather than on performance.

The uploaded field names are unchanged and keep `gen_worker`: they are live OpenSearch columns with baseline history, and renaming one would fork every `gen_only` series and discard its baselines. They describe the gen *worker*, which emits them — not the `gen_only` *mode*. Because `s_test_case_name` is a match key and carries the mode as its prefix, `e2e` and `gen_only` share a **column** but never a **baseline series**. Two module-local constants are renamed to match the widened scope (`GEN_ONLY_DEVICE_STEP_TIME_METRICS` → `DEVICE_STEP_TIME_METRICS`, `GEN_ONLY_PERF_METRIC_LOG_QUERIES` → `DEVICE_STEP_TIME_LOG_QUERIES`); no field name changes.

### A latent wrong-number bug fixed first

The scan accepted `start_offsets` but **no end bound**, so it always read to EOF. Since the parse is deferred until after teardown (so it never reads a still-flushing NFS log), a mode with more than one client would give client 0 a mean averaged over *every later client's* iterations.

This is **latent, not live**: all CI disagg configs carry exactly one `concurrency_list` value and the generator rejects more. But it is silently wrong rather than absent, and plain-pytest local runs do allow several — and widening the family to `e2e`, the mode that sweeps concurrency, is what would have made it reachable.

Each client's window now ends at the **next** client's pre-launch offset snapshot. Taking the bound there rather than at the previous client's return is what makes it safe: the snapshot is the first byte of the next client's segment, so it cannot exclude an iteration the previous client drove, however late the worker flushed it. The last client reads to EOF; a line straddling the bound is dropped (one row out of hundreds, and it belongs to the earlier client). The scan now reads bytes and decodes per line so the accounting matches the `os.path.getsize()` bounds exactly — a text stream cannot be asked its position mid-iteration (`TextIOWrapper.tell` raises *"telling position disabled by next() call"*), and re-encoding a decoded line does not reliably recover its byte length.

**With one client `end_offsets` is `None`, i.e. byte-identical to before** — so the live `gen_only` lane is provably unaffected.

### Test coverage for this part

`tests/unittest/scripts/test_perf_sanity_helpers.py` (43 tests, all passing offline): per-mode upload for `gen_only`/`e2e`/`e2e_time_breakdown` and omission when `benchmark_mode` is `None` (the `ctx_only`/aggregated call site); the gating contract as an executable assertion; and four window cases — confining a client to its own segment, unbounded reads still spanning everything, a bound past EOF degrading harmlessly, and a straddling line dropped. Plus invalid-UTF-8 and CRLF coverage, since moving the decode is the one behavioural difference the binary read introduces. **Mutation-tested**: reverting either half of the `end_offsets` plumbing fails exactly the intended tests and nothing else.

### Accepted side effect

`e2e` teardown now calls `wait_for_gen_log_sentinels()`, which it did not before — a bounded `GEN_LOG_SENTINEL_TIMEOUT = 120` s wait whose timeout path still parses the current contents. Worst case is +120 s on an `e2e` teardown, never a failure. That is the deliberate cost of not reading a still-flushing NFS log (nvbugs 6487036 / 6487040 / 6487038).

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The shipped `time_breakdown.py` does **not** correct the per-worker clock base, so its per-step/per-chunk plots for a *disagg* run are affected by the same offsets fixed here (one worker measured +377680 s). Worth a separate bug; this PR does not change that tool's plotting path.

- [x] `ruff` and `ruff-format` (pinned `v0.9.4`, the hooks that apply to these files — none are in `legacy-files.txt`) run clean over all touched files; remaining hooks left to CI

items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Added per-plan FlashInfer workspaces for persistent CUDA-graph plans.
- Preserved the shared workspace for eager execution and non-persistent plans.
- Shared each plan workspace across CUDA-graph batch-size metadata copies.
- Planned persistent CUDA-graph wrappers during `prepare()` before graph capture.
- Preserved deferred planning for eager multi-wrapper execution.
- Added `PlanWorkspaceKey` and `FlashInferWrappers.workspace_buffer`.
- Each persistent plan kind adds 320 MiB. Gemma3 global and sliding-window plans add 640 MiB total.
- No public API or configuration changes were introduced.
- No configuration or test-list files changed.

## QA Engineer Review

- Added CUDA tests for workspace isolation, workspace reuse, allocation counts, planning before graph capture, eager planning behavior, and replay correctness.
- Updated the spec-decode wrapper fixture to provide its workspace buffer.
- 17 unit tests pass.
- The changed tests are not listed in `test-db/` or `qa/` based on the provided change summary.
- Verdict: needs follow-up to confirm CI or manual-QA test-list coverage.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->


  ## Description

  FlashInfer `plan()` stores schedule data in its workspace buffer. Multiple persistent attention plan kinds previously shared the same buffer. Planning a later wrapper could overwrite
  schedule data required by an earlier wrapper. CUDA graph replay does not execute Python planning again, so the captured kernels could consume overwritten schedule data and produce
  incorrect outputs.

  This change:

  - Allocates a separate workspace for every persistent CUDA-graph plan kind.
  - Keeps the original shared workspace for eager execution and non-persistent plans, including custom attention masks and multi-item scoring.
  - Ensures persistent and non-persistent CUDA-graph plans never use the same physical buffer.
  - Shares the per-plan workspace registry across CUDA-graph batch-size metadata copies, so allocation depends on the number of plan kinds rather than the number of graph replicas.
  - Plans all persistent CUDA-graph wrappers during `prepare()` before graph capture.
  - Preserves the existing deferred planning behavior for eager multi-wrapper execution.

  There are no public API or configuration changes.

  Each persistent CUDA-graph plan kind adds one 320 MiB workspace allocation. Gemma3 uses global and sliding-window plan kinds, adding 640 MiB in total. CUDA-graph batch-size replicas reuse
  these buffers and do not add further allocations.

  ## Test Coverage

  - `pytest -q tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_flashinfer_attention.py`
    - Result: `17 passed`
    - Verifies distinct workspaces for global and sliding-window plans.
    - Verifies persistent plans do not alias custom-mask or multi-item plan workspaces.
    - Verifies CUDA-graph batch-size replicas reuse the same per-plan buffers.
    - Verifies allocation count equals the number of persistent plan kinds.
    - Verifies eager execution retains the shared workspace behavior.
    - Verifies all CUDA-graph wrappers are planned before capture.
    - Verifies CUDA-graph replay output matches eager execution.

  - Gemma3-27B FP8 accuracy test with FlashInfer and CUDA graphs enabled:
    - Before fix: `44.6667%` (`402/900`)
    - After fix: `50.7778%` (`457/900`)
    - Improvement: `6.1111` percentage points
    Note: although test still passes the accuracy test without this fix on Blackwell, applying the fix consistently improves accuracy by about 6%. On Rubin, however, the accuracy requirement will not be met without this fix.

items.title: [None][infra] Add perf-analyze and perf-optimize skills to agent-flow
items.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #18330, which vendored the `perf-analyze` and `perf-optimize`
workflows but deliberately held back the two operator skills that go with
them:

> The operator skills are not ported: they hardcode one site's cluster,
> partition and image registry.

Without them, an agent asked to diagnose or optimize a `trtllm-serve`
deployment hand-rolls its own serve → benchmark → profile loop and the
vendored workflows go unused — the skill `description` is what makes Claude
Code reach for the workflow in the first place.

This ports both skills, minus the environment setup section that was the
reason to hold them back. Allocating a GPU node, launching the container and
building the wheel are cluster-specific steps an operator already has a
recipe for, and no wording of them generalizes across sites — so rather than
shipping a `<placeholder>` template nobody can run as written, that section
is simply dropped. What each skill keeps is what is specific to *driving its
workflow*:

- **Preflight** — CLI installed, required paths exist, git preconditions
  (`perf-optimize` needs a clean checkout and a branch; `perf-analyze` is
  read-only with respect to the TRT-LLM checkout).
- **Authoring `task.yaml`** — every field, which are required, and the
  defaults. Including the per-measurement cost estimate that is the #1
  launch trap for `perf-optimize`: a measurement that cannot finish inside
  one allocation restarts forever and the campaign never completes.
- **Launch / monitor / wrap up** — the run is long, so it is backgrounded;
  what the progress output means, and which artifacts to point the user at.
- **Pitfalls** — resume semantics after a walltime kill (each workflow
  resumes from its own `.perf_{analyze,optimize}_state.json`), and that
  partition-level `DenyQos` — not the QoS list on your account — is what
  usually decides the walltime ceiling.

Also updates two things the port makes stale:

- The `perf-optimize` README note still said the skill was "not vendored
  here"; it now links to it and states what it does and does not cover.
- The preflight install hint points at `<trtllm_repo_path>/agent-flow` —
  the copy in the checkout being tested — rather than upstream agent-flow,
  so an operator cannot end up running stale workflow code against these
  instructions.

Markdown only, all of it under `agent-flow/`. No TensorRT-LLM runtime,
kernel, API or Python code is changed.

## Test Coverage

No new code paths, so no new tests — both files are operator documentation
consumed by Claude Code, and `agent-flow/tests/` pins no skill contents
(the tests that did were dropped alongside the skills in #18330).

Verified that the existing suite is unaffected:

```bash
cd agent-flow && pip install -e '.[test]' && pytest tests/
# 993 passed in 53.14s
```

Also checked by hand that the port left no dangling references: the state
filename in each skill matches its workflow's `state.py` `STATE_FILENAME`,
and no section removed with the environment steps is still cross-referenced.

items.title: [TRTLLMINF-374][infra] BoltProfileGen: log SLURM queue-vs-run timing
items.body:
## Summary
A SLURM job's Blue Ocean stage duration lumps queue wait and actual run time
together — Jenkins can't see inside the scheduler — so an oversubscribed cluster
(long queue) is indistinguishable from a genuinely slow job.

- After each SLURM job reaches a terminal state, log a single `[TIMING]` line
  splitting queue wait (Start−Submit) from run time (End−Start), parsed from
  `sacct`.
- Diagnostic only: the helper swallows any sacct/date error and never fails the
  stage.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

- Logs queue wait time (`Start−Submit`), execution time (`End−Start`), and total duration after terminal job completion.
- Uses `sacct` data and date parsing to calculate timing values.
- Swallows `sacct` and date-parsing errors so timing diagnostics cannot fail the pipeline stage.
- No public or exported entities changed.

items.title: [#17913][fix] Prevent PyTorch executor crash when forward step is absorbed
items.body:
## Description

_forward_step returns `None` when a forward is absorbed after a failure, but both PyTorch executor loops dereferenced it and the exception escaped the loop, taking down serving. This change treats `None` as no outputs for this iteration, skipping sampling while keeping required collectives and previous-batch processing.

Fixes #17913.

## Test Coverage

- Added CPU-only regression tests for both executor paths (non-overlap and overlap) verifying skipped sampling and continued response flushing after a `None` forward.
- `python -m compileall -q tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/py_executor.py tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_py_executor.py` and `git diff --check` pass.
